lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Ensure the code-profile URL is clickable and leads directly to a polished profile or portfolio.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to reach the work directly.

items.says: Replace `example.com` if it appears on the actual résumé.
items.because: A recognizable platform or personal domain is preferable.

items.says: Consider adding LinkedIn if the profile is current and useful.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for US applications.
items.because: They raise privacy and discrimination concerns, and nationality does not establish work authorization.

items.says: Standardize the date punctuation.
items.because: It should match the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Check that the degree name matches the university’s official terminology.
Add a strong GPA or directly relevant research, thesis, or courses if helpful.
items.because: These details should support the targeted ML or agent roles.

items.says: Replace `Country` with the actual country.
items.because: It is a placeholder rather than a location.

items.says: Match the master’s entry’s date style and location formatting.
Add a strong GPA, honors, or relevant distinctions if applicable.
Consider a brief industry descriptor if the company is not widely known.
items.because: It would help readers understand the organization.

items.says: Define what the 35% improvement represents.
items.because: It could mean a relative improvement, a percentage-point improvement, or error reduction.

items.says: Identify the baseline and evaluation set.
items.because: They would make the accuracy figure credible.

items.says: Clarify what diagnostic accuracy measures if it is not ordinary classification accuracy.
State precisely how the drop from 14% to 6% is measured.
items.because: The wording implies an eight-percentage-point reduction but leaves room for ambiguity.

items.says: Explain how disagreement was measured or give the number of cases if space allows.
Simplify the sentence.
items.because: It asks readers to track specialists, a reviewer, signal restrictions, and an outcome at once.

items.says: Verify that restricting the independent reviewer’s signals is accurate.
items.because: A reviewer is often expected to have broader visibility.

items.says: Add the missing grammatical connector before the 18% reduction.
Change `penalises` to US English.
items.because: The résumé targets US roles and otherwise uses US conventions.

items.says: Define the evaluation conditions behind `equal accuracy`.
items.because: Readers need to know whether the comparison used the same held-out set or operating threshold.

items.says: Make GRPO understandable to readers unfamiliar with the acronym when targeting less technical roles.
Shorten implementation detail if the bullet wraps across four lines.
Clarify how citation quality was measured.
items.because: Citation evaluation is not obviously connected to industrial diagnostics.

items.says: Add a serial comma.
items.because: It would improve punctuation consistency.

items.says: State whether the harness entered CI or remained in use, if it did.
items.because: The current wording can sound like a one-time script.

items.says: Clarify what `before release` refers to.
items.because: It could mean production release or an internal experiment.

items.says: Delete or merge the second assistant-only loss-masking bullet.
items.because: It repeats the method in the diagnostic-accuracy bullet without a separate quantified result.

items.says: Make the claim about reproducing tool outputs technically precise.
items.because: A model normally learns assistant responses conditioned on tool outputs, not necessarily the outputs themselves.

items.says: Move the backlog bullet to the first or second position.
items.because: It shows deployed product impact and operational scale.

items.says: Clarify whether the 800-plus signals are raw signals, derived features, or both.
Give the comparison point for the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: Readers need to assess whether other operational changes contributed.

items.says: Verify that `Junior` is the official title.
items.because: An official title should not be unnecessarily downgraded or modified.

items.says: The attribution of a fourfold GPU-memory reduction to BF16 alone is technically implausible.
items.because: BF16 generally halves storage for affected FP32 tensors, so other contributing changes would need to be reflected.

items.says: Specify which memory measurement fell fourfold.
items.because: Peak allocated, peak reserved, and model-state memory are different measures.

items.says: Add the practical result of the memory reduction if true.
items.because: It could show whether training fit on smaller GPUs or supported a larger batch.

items.says: Clarify the workload or concurrency level behind the p95 measurement if available.
Confirm that caching preserved result freshness and correctness.
items.because: Cache invalidation may invite questions.

items.says: Fix the tense mismatch between `Maintained` and `adds`.
items.because: One is past tense and the other is present tense.

items.says: Clarify whether release cycles shortened to or by three days.
Add the prior release-cycle duration if available.
items.because: Without it, the size of the improvement is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether you created the automated checks or only maintained them.
Verify that the 30 items were separate services rather than scheduled jobs.
Quantify the eliminated backlog or dispatch delay if data is available.
Prevent `dead-letter` from splitting across lines in the final PDF.
items.because: Forced word breaks can interfere with ATS extraction.

items.says: Replace `Owner` with a more accurate conventional role designation.
items.because: `Owner` can sound vague for an open-source or personal project.

items.says: Add a repository link if the project is public.
List concrete runtime technologies instead of only the broad field of multi-agent systems.
Ensure `Present` is accurate when submitting.
Replace or delete the AI-first engineering-practices bullet.
items.because: Its delivery and outcomes claims lack evidence, scale, or a clear account of what was built.

items.says: Define what the raw conversation’s 100-fold growth is measured against.
State how you checked that compaction preserved necessary information.
items.because: The bullet does not establish that quality or task performance held up.

items.says: Define what the 10K-token limit covers.
items.because: It could refer to each model call, the active prompt, or stored state.

items.says: Clarify where the deadlocks and lost results were observed or reproduced.
items.because: They could have appeared in production, a stress test, or automated testing.

items.says: Add a durability measure if available.
items.because: Repeated failure-free runs or a CI regression test would substantiate the fix.

items.says: Make `50-way fan-out` understandable in the project documentation.
Add a project or repository link if public.
Clarify elsewhere in the entry whether `Contributor` means accepted upstream contributions.
Consider naming more specific evaluation areas in the technology field.
items.because: They may be central to the targeted roles.

items.says: Say whether you implemented the metrics, integrated existing implementations, or both.
Mention accepted pull requests, releases, or test coverage if applicable.
items.because: They make the open-source contribution more verifiable.

items.says: Name a few important metrics if they are recognized and relevant.
items.because: A count alone does not identify them.

items.says: Name the exact Kendall statistic, likely Kendall’s tau.
items.because: `Kendall correlation` is imprecise.

items.says: Give statistical significance or uncertainty if analyzed.
Explain how degradation severity was ordered and how the 400-plus trials were distributed.
items.because: The number of reports or degradation levels is unclear.

items.says: Use more precise terminology than `report-level trials` if reports generated multiple corrupted variants.
Delete the backlog bullet from the Research-Agent project.
items.because: It nearly duplicates the internship accomplishment and is unrelated to research-agent evaluation.

items.says: Move Git out of `Programming`.
items.because: Git is a version-control tool, not a programming language.

items.says: Separate frameworks from methods or concepts.
items.because: PyTorch is a framework, while LoRA and GRPO are techniques.

items.says: Make `agent evaluation` more specific.
items.because: The phrase is broad and difficult to assess.

items.says: Add relevant tools demonstrated elsewhere if you have meaningful proficiency.
items.because: The skills list could better reflect model-serving, experiment-tracking, data, container, or cloud work.

items.says: Use one date format and dash style throughout.
items.because: The résumé’s formatting should be consistent.

items.says: Shorten dense bullets to roughly two lines where possible.
items.because: Several bullets slow scanning.

items.says: Order bullets by impact across entries.
items.because: Deployed outcomes should precede technical methods and supporting infrastructure.
